subject.title: fix(acp): keep completed run-mode sessions resumable

question: Do ACP owners accept retaining terminal one-shot metadata under the new capability-and-readiness gates without additional live crash-window or cross-platform proof?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well tested, but it intentionally reverses cleanup behavior for a subset of persisted terminal sessions, and only repository owners can accept that lifecycle and upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the gated lifecycle
options.body: Approve the current capability, identity, readiness, backend-pinning, and fail-closed gates and merge after exact-head checks remain green.

options.title: Require crash-window proof
options.body: Hold merge until a live gateway restart or forced process-loss scenario demonstrates that retained one-shots resume once without stale delivery or duplicate completion.

options.title: Keep one-shots terminal
options.body: Reject retained one-shot metadata and require users needing guaranteed follow-ups to use persistent ACP sessions instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the gated lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the current capability, identity, readiness, backend-pinning, and fail-closed gates and merge after exact-head checks remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP lifecycle and sessions_send product review makes this the strongest available owner for accepting the compatibility boundary.
